data: Civilian DOS-4 station — hosted Soyuz 17 (29 days) + Soyuz 18 (63 days, then-longest spaceflight) crews; deorbited 1977-02-03

The fourth civilian Salyut (DOS-4), built by the Korolev bureau and operated by the Soviet civilian space programme rather than the military Almaz line. Launched 1974-12-26 on a Proton-K, Salyut 4 carried a 25-cm OST-1 solar telescope, an X-ray telescope, and a complement of life-sciences experiments. Hosted two long-duration crews: Soyuz 17 (Gubarev + Grechko, 29 days, 1975-01-11 to 1975-02-09) and Soyuz 18 (Klimuk + Sevastyanov, 63 days, 1975-05-24 to 1975-07-26, then the longest crewed spaceflight in history). A third attempt — Soyuz 18a (Lazarev + Makarov, 1975-04-05) — suffered a 21-g booster failure during launch, returning the crew safely after the highest-ever landing g-load survived by humans. Salyut 4 hosted Soyuz 20, an automated dog/biological-experiment 3-month visit, before re-entering on 1977-02-03 after 26 months.

Salyut 4 was where the civilian station line finally found its feet. A DOS science station, it worked reliably where earlier stations had failed — hosting two crews, one for 29 days and one for 63, and carrying a solar telescope and a full science program. After the deadly start of Salyut 1 and the on-orbit failures that followed, Salyut 4 was the quiet proof that the Soviet Union could now keep a station and its crews healthy and productive for weeks at a time.
Second Almaz military station — Soyuz 14 crew Jul 1974; Soyuz 15 failed automatic docking; reportedly tested an onboard cannon 1975-01-24
First Almaz military station — depressurised on orbit before any crew arrived; reentered 1973-05-28 after 54 days
Last Almaz military station — Soyuz 21 + Soyuz 24 crews; Soyuz 23 failed approach; reentered 1977-08-08 after 412 days
